title: Hosted API Rollout Gates and Thresholds
author: Elliot Price
body:
h1. Purpose
Define the SRE-owned gates used to decide whether a Hosted API model rollout can proceed, pause, or rollback. These gates are designed to catch both hard failures and early warning signals.

h1. Applicability
These gates apply to production traffic on Hosted API routes managed by routerd. For Dedicated or Private, see environment-specific SLO docs.

h1. Canary duration minimums
Minimum hold times are non-negotiable unless there is a declared incident with an explicit mitigation plan.
* 1% canary: minimum 45 minutes
* 5%: minimum 30 minutes
* 25%: minimum 60 minutes
* 50%: minimum 60 minutes

h1. Proceed / Pause / Rollback gates
Gates are evaluated relative to the current stable version for the same route and time-of-day window.

h2. Availability
* Proceed: route-level success rate is within 0.05% absolute of baseline.
* Pause: success rate worse than baseline by 0.05% to 0.15% absolute for >= 10 minutes.
* Rollback: success rate worse than baseline by > 0.15% absolute for >= 5 minutes, or any sustained 5xx spike with clear correlation to the canary version.

h2. Latency
Evaluate p95 end-to-end latency at the gateway and p95 model runtime latency.
* Proceed: p95 gateway latency delta <= +8% and p95 runtime latency delta <= +10%.
* Pause: p95 gateway delta +8% to +15% or runtime delta +10% to +20% for >= 10 minutes.
* Rollback: p95 gateway delta > +15% for >= 5 minutes, or streaming time-to-first-token delta > +20% for >= 10 minutes.

h2. Saturation and capacity
* Pause if any of the following persist >= 10 minutes:
  - GPU queue depth above the route-specific normal band
  - request timeouts rising while GPU utilization is > 90%
  - scheduler rejects increasing (capacity mismatch)
* Rollback if saturation causes customer-visible errors (429/5xx) above the availability rollback gate.

h2. Cost regression (guardrail)
Cost is a guardrail gate, not a hard blocker, unless it risks customer billing correctness.
* Pause if cost per 1k tokens increases by > 12% for >= 30 minutes with no prior approval.
* Rollback if token accounting differs materially (billing drift) or if the model emits abnormal tokenization behavior (suspected tokenizer mismatch).

h1. Error budget constraints
Rollouts MUST NOT start if the Hosted API service is currently in error budget burn (SLO burn alerts firing) unless the rollout is an approved mitigation.

h1. How to record gate decisions
The driver MUST paste the following into the tracking ticket at each ramp step:
* current traffic %
* canary version and stable version IDs
* links to dashboards
* explicit statement: proceed / pause / rollback
* short rationale (1-3 sentences)

h1. Notes on noisy metrics
* If baseline is unstable due to unrelated traffic anomalies, pause the rollout and wait for baseline stabilization.
* For low-volume routes, use longer windows and focus on error types rather than aggregate error rate.
